life_history: Nick is a teenage student and aspiring soccer player who recently engaged in experimental alcohol use. The counseling session was precipitated by his completion of the CRAFFT questionnaire, which flagged potential risks. He recently snuck out with a friend to drink beer in a park and narrowly avoided getting in trouble with a police officer. Nick is highly motivated by his athletic goals, hoping to play college soccer and earn a scholarship, but faces peer pressure as some of his friends drink.
core_belief_description: I am a failure, a loser
intermediate_beliefs: Positive assumption: If I drink occasionally with friends, then I can fit in and have fun; negative assumption: If I stop drinking entirely, then I will be alienated from my peers and miss out.
intermediate_beliefs_during_depression: If I make a mistake and lose my chance at a soccer scholarship, it proves I have no willpower and my future is ruined.
coping_strategies: Maladaptive coping includes sneaking out, hiding evidence (throwing beers in bushes), and defensively downplaying his actions ('only tried drinking once or twice'). Adaptive coping involves leaning into his intrinsic motivation for soccer, engaging in psychoeducation, and committing to read materials about the risks of addiction.

cognitive_models.situation: Drinking beer in the park with a friend when a police officer comes by.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: We are going to get caught. If my mom finds out about this, she would kill me.
cognitive_models.behavior: Threw the beers in the bushes to hide the evidence and avoided getting a ticket.

cognitive_models.situation: The counselor brings up the health risks of alcohol and offers to share information.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I am not sure if this information is for me since I have only been drinking once or twice. A couple of my friends drink too.
cognitive_models.behavior: Downplays the frequency of his drinking and rationalizes his experimental behavior.

cognitive_models.situation: The counselor explains how alcohol could interfere with his sports goals and brain development.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I really didn't think about how this would affect me playing sports. I want to play soccer in college and get scholarships. I don't wanna become addicted.
cognitive_models.behavior: Shifts to change talk, agrees to take and read the educational materials, and commits to prioritizing his athletic goals.
